quote: I'm gonna need a new roof. So
stewart_read: Customer states he needs a new roof as his reason for solar interest. The schema's template calls for an explicit bridge naming Ion's in-house roofing team and framing solar-plus-roof as a combined opportunity. The rep says only 'We can can definitely help you out there' — vague, no named service, no bridge.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep could be intentionally deferring the roofing conversation to the specialist since setter scope should not sell — but the schema's cross_sell guidance explicitly wants the setter to name the bridge live ('Ion actually does roofing in-house... Want me to have our roofing team take a look?'), which never happens here even briefly.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to name the in-house roofing service explicitly in the moment — a single sentence captures the cross-sell signal for both roofing and solar without any scope creep.

quote: solar roofs, so I don't know what that looks like. It looks like they have their own shingles that are solar panels, and then they they have, like, a hub that they store energy in.
stewart_read: Customer is describing Tesla Solar Roof tiles with an integrated battery — a product Ion does not sell. The rep never corrects this expectation ('Exactly. You're you're kinda just doing your research. Okay.'), leaving the customer's mental model of what he'll be offered fundamentally wrong.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep didn't catch the product mismatch because he was moving fast through verify items. Strategic read would require an explanation elsewhere in the call that reframes Ion's offering — none exists.
coaching_implication: Flag for the rep: when a customer describes shingle-integrated solar with a storage hub, that is Tesla Solar Roof language, a product Ion does not carry. This should be gently reframed here, and at minimum written into the handoff brief so the closer isn't blindsided by an expectation mismatch.

stewart_read: Bill figure is captured but the rep's response is a throwaway acknowledgment with zero flip toward alignment-against-the-utility. Per bill_anchoring, capture without flip is 'necessary but not sufficient' and this is exactly that failure pattern.
alternative_hypothesis: None — this is unambiguous. The rep had a live $250/month figure and the very next line pivoted to the bill-collection logistics without using the number.
coaching_implication: Direct, specific coaching moment: replay this exact 3-second exchange with the rep and show where the flip line should have gone (e.g., naming that $250/month adds up over years, before pivoting to bill collection).

quote: Joshua. Is there anyone else on the title with you?
stewart_read: Rep correctly runs the co-owner check per protocol. Customer answers 'Nope. Just I' (likely a diarization artifact for 'Just me' but attributed to rep — treating cautiously). Rep does not need to invoke spouse_decision protocol since none was disclosed.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed here — correct procedural step, correctly logged. Included to show the verify section was run, not skipped.

quote: I just bought the house April 16.
stewart_read: New homeowner (bought April 16) who is already planning a roof replacement and exploring solar — a customer at the start of a long tenure with active home-improvement plans, a strong qualification signal (long planned tenure + roof timing alignment). The rep treats this purely as an obstacle to bill-history collection ('No. You're all good. You just moved in.') rather than noting it as a positive signal.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to recognize and verbally reinforce these signals — a brand-new homeowner already lining up a roof replacement is a stronger lead than the flat verify-tone conveys; this should be flagged for the closer explicitly.

quote: I'll just have my specialist give you a callback, to go over this information with you
stewart_read: A day and rough time window (tomorrow afternoon, ~2:30) are set, which is better than nothing, but the button-up lacks the full handshake: no one-hour block statement, no no-driving/computer instruction, no explicit 'is that fair?' confirmation, and no promise of a text follow-up.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as acceptable given the short call length — but the schema treats these as hard-required button_up elements regardless of call length, so the omission stands as a gap rather than context-justified compression.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close every call with the full button-up sequence: hour-block statement, sit-down/no-driving expectation, the 'is that fair?' handshake, and a same-call promise of a confirmation text.
